tour.setup.1.text: You are in training: participants are simulated and nothing is recorded for the study.

tour.setup.2.text: Step 1: open the stage. In a real session, then share this window, and only this window, in the video call.

tour.setup.3.text: Step 2: in a real session, choose the backup file here. For training, this is already done.

tour.setup.4.text: Step 3: start the audio recording, then set the sync mark.

tour.setup.5.text: When the steps are done, Go starts the session clock.

tour.run.1.text: Times are only shown on the console: elapsed since Go, current step, total time. An overrun is shown but blocks nothing.

tour.run.2.text: This is where the simulated participants' words appear, with a few tips. Read, then act in the console.

tour.run.3.text: Click a participant who leaves or comes back: the counts depend on it.

tour.run.4.text: Pause freezes the countdowns. Technical incident logs the time of an incident in one click.

tour.run.5.text: When the phase is over, move to the next one here.

tour.tuto.1.text: The tutorial has three steps: vocabulary, a placement demonstration, and each participant's equipment survey.

tour.tuto.2.text: The preview shows what participants see on the shared stage.

tour.tri.1.text: Place the thumbnail in the box the group names: keys 1 to 4, a click on a button or on a box in the preview.

tour.tri.2.text: If there is disagreement, add a second thumbnail (S), then enter the counts per box.

tour.tri.3.text: Ask the ritual question, then "Question asked" (Q). "Next card" (N) only unlocks after that.

tour.tri.4.text: If a participant cannot read well, zoom the large card and pick the region to enlarge.

tour.tri.5.text: The keys useful in this phase are listed here.

tour.disc.1.text: Cards to discuss come in order of severity: Impossible first, then Difficult.

tour.disc.2.text: After the discussion, go to the next card (N).

tour.jug.1.text: Each adapted thumbnail starts from the original's position.

tour.jug.2.text: Move it: left and right arrows for one zone, keys 1 to 4 for a box, or drag in the preview.

tour.jug.3.text: Confirm each adapted thumbnail (Enter). "Next card" unlocks when everything is confirmed.

tour.jug.4.text: The original's marker is visible on the console; R also shows it to participants.

tour.alert.1.text: A banner flags a problem during the session. The banner's button fixes it; nothing is lost in the meantime.

tour.fin.1.text: Your review: each point to review comes with a tip. You can start again as many times as you need.

pres.01.t.context: Titre de l'étape 1 de la présentation

pres.01.b.text: The console stays with the moderator: it controls everything. The stage is the only window shared in the video call: participants only see the card and the four boxes.

pres.02.b.text: At start, choose the day's FG. The tool loads the cards in the right language and runs its own checks: cards, presentation order, font, window.

pres.03.b.text: 1. Open the stage and share it. 2. Choose the backup file: the log is written to it continuously. 3. Start the audio recording and set the mark. Then Go.

pres.04.b.text: After Go: elapsed time, step countdown and total time. An overrun is shown as "+ mm:ss" but blocks nothing. Pause freezes the countdowns.

pres.05.b.text: Present the vocabulary, show a placement on the calibration card, then record each participant's device and smallest readable line.

pres.06.b.text: The group says which box the card goes in. Place the thumbnail: keys 1 to 4, a click, or drag in the preview. The four boxes are empty for every new card.

pres.07.b.text: Add a second thumbnail (S) in the other box, then enter how many participants chose each box.

pres.08.b.text: Ask "Would anyone place it somewhere else?", then "Question asked" (Q). "Next card" (N) only unlocks after that. There is no going back.

pres.09.b.text: If someone cannot read well, zoom the large card to 150 or 200% and choose the region. A mini-map shows participants which part is enlarged.

pres.10.b.text: Only cards placed in Difficult or Impossible are discussed, from most to least severe. The stage shows the adapted version of the exercise.

pres.11.b.text: The adaptation starts from the original's position. Move it as the group says (arrows for one zone, 1 to 4 for a box), then confirm with Enter.

pres.12.b.text: If the backup fails or the stage closes, a banner appears with the button that fixes it. After a crash, reopen the console: "Resume" carries on without losing anything.

pres.13.b.text: "End the session" writes the final file. A copy without the notes can be exported for sharing.

pres.14.b.text: From the start screen, "Practise" runs a simulated focus group: participants who speak, staged incidents, a guided tour and a review at the end. Nothing is recorded for the study.

memo.before.1.text: Choose the FG; check "Cards loaded: 11 of 11".

memo.before.2.text: Open the stage, then share it alone in Zoom or Teams (never the console).

memo.before.4.text: Start the audio recording, then "Set the mark". Then Go.

memo.during.1.text: One card: place, then "Question asked" (Q), then "Next card" (N).

memo.during.2.text: Disagreement: second thumbnail (S) and counts; the total equals those present.

memo.during.3.text: Someone leaves or comes back: click the participant in Present.

memo.during.4.text: Never recall previous judgements; never any name in the notes.

memo.during.5.text: Times are only on the console; an overrun blocks nothing.

memo.inc.scene.do.text: "Open the stage", then share the window again.

memo.inc.save.do.text: "Choose a new file" (or "Degraded mode"). Nothing is lost.

memo.inc.crash.do.text: Reopen the console, "Resume", accept the permission, reopen the stage.

memo.inc.tech.do.text: "Technical incident" logs the time; "Pause" if needed.

memo.after.1.text: File the final file (and the copy without notes) in the FG folder.

memo.after.2.text: Report any warning seen at start to the team.
